(Medicine) Scabies, Superficial fungal i.question: ১) Tinea unguium involves.....?
(Medicine) Scabies, Superficial fungal i.exp:
Tinea unguium is a fungal infection of the nails, also known as onychomycosis.

  • Tinea unguium → Nail

  • Tinea capitis → Scalp

  • Tinea cruris → Groin

  • Tinea corporis → Trunk/body

Exam pearl:
“Tinea unguium → Nail.”

(Medicine) Scabies, Superficial fungal i.question: ২) Which disease is characterized by Auspitz sign?
(Medicine) Scabies, Superficial fungal i.exp:
Auspitz sign is classically seen in psoriasis. It refers to pinpoint bleeding that occurs when the scales of a psoriatic plaque are gently removed.

  • Psoriasis → Auspitz sign

  • Scabies → burrows, intense nocturnal itching

  • Eczema → oozing, crusting, pruritus

  • Tinea → annular lesions with active borders

Exam pearl:
“Auspitz sign = Psoriasis.”

(Medicine) Scabies, Superficial fungal i.question: ৩) Which is not true about ringworm infection?
(Medicine) Scabies, Superficial fungal i.exp:
Ringworm (tinea) typically presents with:

  • Ring-shaped lesions

  • Central clearing

  • Fungal elements visible on microscopy (KOH preparation)

“More intense itching” is not a defining feature of ringworm and can vary considerably depending on the site and type of infection.

Exam pearl:
“Ringworm → Annular lesion + central clearing + fungal hyphae on KOH.”

(Medicine) Scabies, Superficial fungal i.question: ৪) The term dermatitis is synonymous to.........?
(Medicine) Scabies, Superficial fungal i.exp:
The terms dermatitis and eczema are often used interchangeably to describe inflammatory conditions of the skin characterized by features such as erythema, itching, and sometimes vesiculation or scaling.

  • Dermatitis ≈ Eczema

  • Scabies → infestation by Sarcoptes scabiei

  • Psoriasis → chronic inflammatory/immune-mediated dermatosis

  • Tinea → dermatophyte fungal infection

Exam pearl:
“Dermatitis = Eczema.”

(Medicine) Scabies, Superficial fungal i.question: ৫) Which is a systemic scabicidal drug?
(Medicine) Scabies, Superficial fungal i.exp:
Ivermectin is a systemic/oral scabicidal drug used to treat scabies, especially in severe, crusted, or difficult-to-treat cases.

  • Ivermectin → systemic (oral) scabicide

  • Permethrin → topical scabicide

  • Crotamiton → topical

  • Benzyl benzoate → topical

Exam pearl:
“Systemic scabicide = Ivermectin.”

(Medicine) Scabies, Superficial fungal i.question: ৬) Which is not a feature of psoriasis?
(Medicine) Scabies, Superficial fungal i.exp:
Psoriasis classically affects the extensor surfaces—especially the elbows and knees, rather than the flexor surfaces.

Typical features:

  • Erythematous plaques

  • Dry, silvery-white scales

  • Well-defined margins

  • Commonly affects extensor surfaces

Exam pearl:
“Psoriasis → Extensor surfaces + silvery scales + well-demarcated plaques.”

(Medicine) Scabies, Superficial fungal i.question: ৭) A boy of 5 years presented with nocturnal itching & multiple papulo vesicular lesion at his finger web. What may be possible diagnosis?
(Medicine) Scabies, Superficial fungal i.exp:
A 5-year-old child with intense nocturnal itching and papulovesicular lesions in the finger webs strongly suggests scabies, caused by the mite Sarcoptes scabiei.

Typical features:

  • Severe itching, worse at night

  • Finger webs are a classic site

  • Papules, vesicles, and burrows

  • In children, the palms, soles, and scalp may also be involved

Exam pearl:
“Nocturnal itching + finger-web lesions → Scabies.”

(Medicine) Scabies, Superficial fungal i.question: ৮) Which is major form of eczema?
(Medicine) Scabies, Superficial fungal i.exp:
Atopic eczema (atopic dermatitis) is considered the major/common form of eczema, especially in children. It is associated with itching, dry skin, and a personal or family history of atopy.

  • Atopic eczema → major/common form

  • Discoid eczema → coin-shaped lesions

  • Seborrhoeic eczema → scalp, face, and seborrhoeic areas

  • Asteatotic eczema → dry, cracked skin, commonly in elderly people

Exam pearl:
“Major form of eczema = Atopic eczema.”

(Medicine) Scabies, Superficial fungal i.question: ৯) Which one is definitive investigation for psoriasis?
(Medicine) Scabies, Superficial fungal i.exp:
Psoriasis is usually diagnosed clinically, but when a definitive/confirmatory investigation is required, a skin biopsy with histopathological examination is used.

Typical histopathological features include:

  • Acanthosis

  • Parakeratosis

  • Munro microabscesses

  • Thinning of suprapapillary plates

Other options:

  • Dermatoscopy → supportive diagnostic tool

  • Patch test → allergic contact dermatitis

  • Phototesting → assessment of photosensitivity

Exam pearl:
“Definitive/confirmatory test for psoriasis → Skin biopsy + histopathology.”

(Medicine) Scabies, Superficial fungal i.question: ১০) What is the 1st step to be taken during drug eruption?
(Medicine) Scabies, Superficial fungal i.exp:
The first and most important step in drug eruption is to stop/omit the offending drug, provided it is clinically safe to do so.

Further management depends on severity:

  • Mild eruption → symptomatic treatment

  • Severe reactions → supportive care ± corticosteroids/other specific treatment

  • Anaphylaxis → emergency treatment with IM adrenaline

Exam pearl:
“Drug eruption → First step = Stop the offending drug.”

(Medicine) Scabies, Superficial fungal i.question: ১১) Which disease can lead to AGN?
(Medicine) Scabies, Superficial fungal i.exp:
Acute glomerulonephritis (AGN) can occur as a complication of streptococcal infection, particularly streptococcal skin infections.

Among the given options, psoriasis itself does not cause AGN. So this MCQ is problematic as written.

The classic skin disease associated with post-streptococcal AGN is impetigo, not scabies, eczema, psoriasis, or tinea.

Exam pearl:
“Post-streptococcal AGN → Pharyngitis or impetigo.”

(Medicine) Scabies, Superficial fungal i.question: ১২) Cardinal features of eczema excludes.....?
(Medicine) Scabies, Superficial fungal i.exp:
The cardinal features of eczema (dermatitis) include:

  • Itching (pruritus) — a hallmark feature

  • Scratching — occurs due to intense itching

  • Dryness of skin (xerosis) — commonly present

Blisters/vesicles can occur in some types of eczema, particularly acute eczema, but they are not a cardinal feature.

Exam pearl:
“Cardinal features of eczema → Itch + scratching + dryness; blisters are not essential.”

(Medicine) Scabies, Superficial fungal i.question: ১৩) Gout can be complicated from which skin disease?
(Medicine) Scabies, Superficial fungal i.exp:
Psoriasis is associated with hyperuricemia and gout in some patients, particularly in extensive or severe disease. Increased epidermal cell turnover leads to increased purine breakdown and uric acid production.

  • Psoriasis → can be associated with gout/hyperuricemia

  • Scabies → parasitic infestation

  • Eczema → inflammatory skin disorder

  • Tinea → fungal infection

Exam pearl:
“Psoriasis → increased cell turnover → ↑ uric acid → risk of gout.”

(Medicine) Scabies, Superficial fungal i.question: ১৪) Scabies is caused by the ........?
(Medicine) Scabies, Superficial fungal i.exp:
Scabies is caused by the Sarcoptes scabiei var. hominis, a microscopic mite that burrows into the skin.

  • Scabies → Mite

  • Lice → Pediculosis

  • Mosquito → vector for diseases such as malaria/dengue

  • Tick → different arthropod; not the cause of scabies

Exam pearl:
“Scabies → Sarcoptes scabiei → Mite.”

(Medicine) Scabies, Superficial fungal i.question: ১৫) A 3 years old girl presented with itching, scaling & erythema in both cheeks with family history of asthma. what will be most probable diagnosis?
(Medicine) Scabies, Superficial fungal i.exp:
Answer: খ) Eczema (Atopic dermatitis)

Difficulty: Easy

Explanation:
A 3-year-old child with itching, scaling, and erythema of the cheeks, plus a family history of asthma, strongly suggests atopic eczema (atopic dermatitis).

Atopic eczema → common in children + pruritus + facial involvement + family history of atopy
Scabies → intense nocturnal itching + burrows/finger webs
Psoriasis → well-demarcated plaques with silvery scales
Tinea → annular lesions with central clearing
Exam pearl:
“Child + itchy facial eczema + family history of asthma → Atopic dermatitis.”

(Medicine) Scabies, Superficial fungal i.question: ১৬) Malassezia furfur infection presents as.......?
(Medicine) Scabies, Superficial fungal i.exp:
Malassezia furfur is a lipophilic yeast that normally inhabits the skin but can proliferate excessively, causing pityriasis (tinea) versicolor. It presents as hypo- or hyperpigmented, finely scaling macules, commonly on the trunk and upper limbs.

High-yield Mycology recall:
Malassezia furfur → Pityriasis versicolor
It is a lipophilic, yeast-like fungus and is associated with increased sweating and humid conditions.

Exam pearl:
“Malassezia makes the skin look multicolored” → Pityriasis versicolor.

(Medicine) Scabies, Superficial fungal i.question: ১৭) Calcipotriol is a mainstay of primary care management of which disease?
(Medicine) Scabies, Superficial fungal i.exp:
Calcipotriol is a synthetic vitamin D₃ analogue that inhibits keratinocyte proliferation and promotes differentiation. It is a commonly used topical treatment for mild-to-moderate plaque psoriasis, often used alone or in combination with a topical corticosteroid.

High-yield Dermatology recall:
Calcipotriol → Psoriasis
Other topical options include corticosteroids, vitamin D analogues, topical retinoids, and calcineurin inhibitors depending on the site and severity.

Exam pearl:
Vitamin D analogue = Calcipotriol = Psoriasis.

(Medicine) Scabies, Superficial fungal i.question: ১৮) Which is also known as athlete’s foot?
(Medicine) Scabies, Superficial fungal i.exp:
Tinea pedis is a dermatophyte infection of the feet and is commonly called athlete’s foot. It typically affects the interdigital spaces and may cause itching, scaling, fissuring, or maceration.

High-yield Dermatology recall:

  • Tinea pedis → Foot → Athlete’s foot

  • Tinea cruris → Groin → Jock itch

  • Tinea capitis → Scalp

  • Tinea unguium → Nails

Exam pearl:
“Pedis = Pedal/foot” → Tinea pedis = Athlete’s foot.

(Medicine) Scabies, Superficial fungal i.question: ১৯) Hypertrichosis may be caused by adverse effect of which drug?
(Medicine) Scabies, Superficial fungal i.exp:
Minoxidil can cause hypertrichosis (excessive hair growth) as an adverse effect, particularly with systemic use. It is a well-known adverse effect of oral minoxidil and may also occur with topical preparations.

High-yield Pharmacology recall:
Minoxidil adverse effects: hypertrichosis, edema, tachycardia, and headache.
Minoxidil is a potassium-channel opener and a potent arteriolar vasodilator; it is also used topically for androgenetic alopecia.

Exam pearl:
Minoxidil → unwanted hair growth (hypertrichosis).

(Medicine) Scabies, Superficial fungal i.question: ২০) Treatment option of atopic eczema excludes.....?
(Medicine) Scabies, Superficial fungal i.exp:
Calcipotriol is not a standard treatment for atopic eczema. It is a vitamin D₃ analogue primarily used in psoriasis. Atopic eczema is managed with emollients, topical corticosteroids, and, when needed, sedating antihistamines for itch-related sleep disturbance.

High-yield Dermatology recall:
Atopic eczema → Emollients + topical corticosteroids
Psoriasis → Calcipotriol

Exam pearl:
Calcipotriol is for psoriasis, not atopic eczema.
